body.statement:
For every regular coherent foldwise fit constrained as in the corrected definition, measure a pointwise matrix error by its conditional \(L^2(P)\) norm.  Then
\[
\{E_P\|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\}^{1/2}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_D+r_B),
\]
\(r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b=O_P(R_\Sigma)\), and
\[
\|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_{L^2(P)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.
\]
The full estimated efficient score \(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U\) has the same linear \(L^2(P)\) stability bound relative to \(U-QU\).
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 H=B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B,
 \qquad \widehat H=\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B. \tag{41}
\]
The observed-cell positivity assumption and the fitted half-margin bound give uniform bounds for \(D^{-1}\) and \(\widehat D^{-1}\).  For any \(v\in\mathbb R^K\), matricizing the vector \(Bv\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{mat}(Bv)=M_A\operatorname{diag}(v)M_Z^{\mathsf T},
\]
and therefore
\[
 \|Bv\|_2=\|M_A\operatorname{diag}(v)M_Z^{\mathsf T}\|_{\mathrm F}
 \geq\sigma_{\min}(M_A)\sigma_{\min}(M_Z)\|v\|_2. \tag{42}
\]
The same calculation applies to \(\widehat B\) under the fitted singular-value half-margins.  Thus \(H^{-1}\) and \(\widehat H^{-1}\) are uniformly bounded.  The exact identities
\[
 \widehat D^{-1}-D^{-1}=\widehat D^{-1}(D-\widehat D)D^{-1},
 \qquad
 \widehat H^{-1}-H^{-1}=\widehat H^{-1}(H-\widehat H)H^{-1} \tag{43}
\]
and telescoping the products in the formula for \(N_B\) give pointwise
\[
 \|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \{\|\widehat D-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat B-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\}. \tag{44}
\]
Taking the declared conditional \(L^2(P)\) norm proves the first assertion.

The data-driven Gram-threshold lemma applies because the projection-Gram gap puts every nonzero eigenvalue of \(G(X)\) above \(\varepsilon\), while the coherent fit uses \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\).  It gives, without using the true rank as a fitted input,
\[
 \|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}-G^+\|_{L^2(P_X;\mathrm{op})}
 \leq26\varepsilon^{-2}r_G,\qquad
 \|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}. \tag{45}
\]
It also shows that \(r_{G,\infty}=o_P(1)\) selects the true rank almost surely in \(x\) with probability tending to one; this is a conclusion of the observable threshold rule, not an oracle constraint.

Apply (43)--(45), together with
\[
 \widehat M^{-1}-M^{-1}=\widehat M^{-1}(M-\widehat M)M^{-1}, \tag{46}
\]
and product telescoping successively to \(R,N,c,h,G,b_U\).  Every factor not differenced is uniformly bounded by fixed \(K\), bounded \(Y\), the true margins, the fitted half-margins, and (45).  Conditional Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}
       \widehat b_{\widehat U}-h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_U\|_2
 &\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma,\\
 \|\widehat N\widehat U-N_BU\|_2
 &\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma. \tag{47}
\end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting the two lines in the definition of \(Q\) proves
\[
 \|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma. \tag{48}
\]
Equations (43), (46), latent positivity, and the two fitted measurement half-margins applied directly to the product bridge give
\[
 \|\widehat U-U\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_m+r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma. \tag{49}
\]
The triangle inequality applied to (48)--(49) proves the same linear bound for
\((\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-(U-QU)\).  Finally, each of \(r_R,r_N,r_h,r_G,r_b\) is controlled by the preceding telescoping identities from its defining coherent plug-in map, or is itself a displayed nonnegative coordinate of \(R_\Sigma\).  Their sum is therefore \(O_P(R_\Sigma)\), as asserted.
body.justification: Pseudoinverse perturbation control is needed to transport nuisance rates into score convergence without differentiating the outcome-density estimator twice.
body.gap: The adjacent bridge papers do not analyze perturbation of this nested posterior and conditional-Gram projector.
body.consumer: It converts rates from a coherent latent-factor fit into consistent standard errors and stable contrast scores.
